blocks.caption: Identification of sulphate radical
rows: Take 3 g of solid sample in a clean test tube. Dissolve it in 5 cm³ of distilled water. Acidify the solution with a few drops of dil. HNO₃ and then add 5 cm³ barium nitrate solution.
A heavy white precipitate of BaSO₄ is formed.

blocks.title: Did you know?
blocks.text: Dilute nitric acid is added to destroy any carbonate ions present in the solution as an impurity.

blocks.prompt: a) Distinguish carbonate (CO₃²⁻) and bicarbonate (HCO₃¹⁻) radicals.
blocks.explanation: Both give effervescence of CO₂ with a dilute acid. The difference: a carbonate solution gives a white precipitate with magnesium sulphate (MgSO₄) in the cold, whereas a bicarbonate gives it only on boiling. Bicarbonates also decompose on heating, giving CO₂.

blocks.prompt: b) What is ring test? Give equation for this test.
blocks.explanation:
It is the brown ring test for nitrate. Fresh FeSO₄ solution is added to the nitrate solution, then concentrated H₂SO₄ is poured slowly down the side of the tube. A brown ring forms where the two layers meet:
NO₃⁻ + 3Fe²⁺ + 4H⁺ → NO + 3Fe³⁺ + 2H₂O
Fe²⁺ + NO → [Fe(NO)]²⁺ (brown ring)

blocks.prompt: c) Give names and formulas of some water insoluble sulphates.
blocks.explanation: Barium sulphate BaSO₄, lead(II) sulphate PbSO₄ and strontium sulphate SrSO₄. Calcium sulphate CaSO₄ is also only very slightly soluble.
